data.title: Three Prachin Buri factories face toxins probe
data.description: Three factories in Prachin Buri have been ordered to suspend operations following suspected toxic chemical leaks that caused water pollution during flooding, while investigations into alleged nominee ownership and “a prominent surname” involved are also under way.

data.title: Deluge by design: Thai villages flooded to protect capital
data.description: AYUTTHAYA - Stilt houses in villages north of Bangkok are no longer high enough to stay dry as Thai authorities deliberately flood riverside communities to spare the capital.

data.title: Chao Phraya Dam discharge rate reduced further
data.description: A gradual reduction in the water discharge rate from the Chao Phraya Dam in Chai Nat from 1,900 to 1,800 cubic metres per second will be completed by 7pm on Wednesday, the Royal Irrigation Department (RID) said.

data.title: Nearly 600 arrests carried out to secure IMF-World Bank meetings
data.description: Police have reported they arrested 587 criminal suspects in provinces beyond Bangkok in the interest of securing the 2026 International Monetary Fund and World Bank Group meetings in the capital.

data.title: Chao Phraya Dam to reduce discharge to 1,800 cu m/sec Wednesday
data.description: The Royal Irrigation Department (RID) has announced a gradual reduction in water discharge from the Chao Phraya Dam in Chai Nat from 1,900 to 1,800 cubic metres per second by 7pm on Wednesday, before maintaining the lower rate.

data.title: Floods persist in Bangkok and 20 provinces
data.description: The Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation reported on Wednesday that floods continued in Bangkok and 20 provinces, mostly in the Central Plains, but their levels were declining.

data.title: Scam crackdowns net 39 suspects
data.description: Police arrested 39 suspects and seized assets worth more than 500 million baht in raids across 11 provinces targeting a transnational scam and money-laundering network.

data.title: Unsit rejects 'shame' jibe over exams
data.description: Interior permanent secretary Unsit Sampuntharat on Tuesday defended the ministry's handling of alleged fraud in local recruitment exams, hitting back at criticism from his predecessor.

data.title: Raid frees exploited Myanmar children
data.description: Authorities have arrested four suspects and rescued children from Myanmar allegedly forced to sell flowers and other goods to tourists in Bangkok.

data.title: Minister targets companies linked to contamination
data.description: Deputy Interior Minister Polapee Suwunchwee on Tuesday vowed legal action against those responsible for a chemical leak from industrial waste that worsened flooding in Si Maha Phot district of Prachin Buri.

data.title: Unsit says flood funds 'sufficient'
data.description: Interior permanent secretary Unsit Sampuntharat on Tuesday assured that the government had sufficient funds to compensate flood victims, with payments already made to nearly 300,000 households.

data.title: Four held in industrial waste seizures
data.description: Authorities in Chon Buri have seized hundreds of tonnes of suspected industrial waste at two sites in the province and detained four people as part of a crackdown on the illegal storage and processing of industrial refuse.

data.title: Suchada faces asset scrutiny
data.description: Bhumjaithai MP Suchada Zhang Thaensap must explain suspected discrepancies in her asset declarations and will receive no legal assistance from the party, its secretary-general Chaichanok Chidchob said on Tuesday.

data.title: PM says text of censure motion hazy
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has criticised the wording of the opposition's no-confidence motion, suggesting it may be why the House speaker has yet to formally notify the government and saying the language may need to be polished to make it more "civilised".

data.title: Light-plane crash in Chon Buri injures pilot
data.description: CHON BURI - The Thai-German pilot was injured when a single-engine light aircraft crashed in Bang Lamung district on Tuesday.

data.title: Suvarnabhumi airport ends free parking for flooded motorists
data.description: Suvarnabhumi airport has advised car owners with flooded homes who parked their vehicles there to remove them immediately, or start paying.

data.title: Top court accepts NBTC chief's appeal
data.description: The Supreme Administrative Court has agreed to rule on an appeal by National Broadcasting and Telecommunications Commission (NBTC) chairman Sarana Boonbaichaiyapruck in a dispute over his eligibility to hold the post.

data.title: Justice minister unaware of details of Thaksin’s amnesty request
data.description: Justice Minister Rutthapon Naowarat said on Tuesday he was unaware of the details of former prime minister Thaksin Shinawatra’s petition seeking an amnesty under the Peaceful Society Promotion Act, and would not be involved.

data.title: No drugs, violence evident in vlogger Hlun Solo's death
data.description: Investigators in Georgia say they have so far found no trace of dangerous substances or evidence suggesting violence in the death of popular Thai travel vlogger Hlun Solo in the capital, Tbilisi, in July.

data.title: Eight districts remain flooded as drainage efforts continue
data.description: Floodwaters have receded in parts of Bangkok, leaving eight districts still affected as authorities continue drainage and cleanup operations.

data.title: Varawut  vows action  over leaks
data.description: Industry Minister Varawut Silpa-archa has pledged strict inspections and immediate closure orders for factories breaking the law following a chemical leak from industrial waste in Prachin Buri that, compounded by flooding, has caused damage and hardship for residents.

data.title: PM confident  of coalition bloc's unity
data.description: Prime Minister and Interior Minister Anutin Charnvirakul yesterday expressed confidence that the ruling coalition would remain united during the upcoming no-confidence debate, saying he trusted coalition partner Pheu Thai to stand by Bhumjaithai (BJT).

data.title: Act now to avoid next 'great repression', IMF says
data.description: Reforms to boost growth, alongside credible tax and spending plans, could help governments avoid a new wave of financial repression, an International Monetary Fund (IMF) official said on Monday.
